doc.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995

title: Army Special Service at Fort Lewis and gigs in Seattle
summary: He served at Fort Lewis 1944-46 playing parades, and worked steadily with Tooty Boyd in Seattle and Portland.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Right. What kind of experience did you have during the war years?

Oh lovely. I was in Fort Lewis, Washington from 1944 to 46, and I was with a Special Service Unit. And we didn’t have to do too much except play for the parades on a Saturday. The rest of the time I was in Seattle.
What did you play for the parades?
What did you play for the parades?
Oh I played glockenspiel sometimes, or I’d take a clarinet out, or a trombone. I had a working knowledge of them you know. I wasn’t good at it but I could fake it pretty good.
And in Seattle, when you were still in the service, what was going on there?

Well I had a job then, yeah, I had a steady job. I worked with a saxophone player by the name of Tooty Boyd who has passed on since then, but we used to drive down to Portland for a job and I had some jobs in Seattle on Jackson Street, which was a hot street in Seattle at that time. So I made more outside of the Army than I made in the Army.
